sources.title: Optical Properties of Multi-Layered Insulation
sources.claim: A representative MLI construction has amber polyimide exterior films backed by aluminum; reflective inner films and low-conductivity spacers form a separate stack.
sources.boundary: The paper describes a common specimen, not a universal layer schedule. Film grade, exposed face, protective coating, layer count and blanket installation remain mission-specific.

sources.title: Basics of Space Flight — Onboard Systems: Temperature Control
sources.claim: NASA explains the gold-colored appearance of familiar thermal blankets as reflective aluminum viewed through amber Kapton.
sources.boundary: Gold color alone does not establish gold metal. This appearance reference does not qualify the workbench blanket for its orbit.

sources.title: Small Spacecraft Technology State of the Art — Thermal Control
sources.claim: The thermal survey distinguishes surface optical properties from MLI effective performance. It lists aluminum, copper and graphite thermal-strap constructions.
sources.boundary: Thermal absorptance and infrared emittance need separate material/process and life evidence. Render color, metalness and roughness are not those properties. A copper dry strap does not imply a copper wetted ammonia line.

sources.title: Satellite Structures — Satellite Structure Panels
sources.claim: The supplier offers honeycomb panels with aluminum or carbon-composite face sheets, alongside structural cylinders, struts and inserts.
sources.boundary: This supports plausible panel and support material families. It does not identify any ODC provider’s alloy, face-sheet gauge, core density or selected supplier.
sources.locator: Satellite Structure Panels; Cones and Cylinders; Struts

sources.title: Satellite Central Structures
sources.claim: The cited sandwich structure combines carbon-fiber composite outer layers with an aluminum honeycomb core.
sources.boundary: A sandwich core is beneath its face sheets. Showing a honeycomb pattern across an intact external panel would misidentify the visible surface; the workbench may show core only in a section or exposed edge.

sources.title: NASA-TM-104622 — Preventing Cracking of Anodized Coatings
sources.claim: Goddard studied clear and dyed-black anodic oxide coatings on aluminum used as spacecraft optical and thermal surfaces.
sources.boundary: Anodizing is a finish over aluminum, not a new bulk metal. Dye, sealing process, contamination and thermal-vacuum durability require selection and verification; a black render does not establish a qualified black finish.

sources.title: Solar Cells Tested on Flexible Array Design
sources.claim: NASA identifies the ROSA deployment members as carbon-fiber composite booms.
sources.boundary: This is evidence for the ROSA technology family. Carbon grade, resin, layup, fiber orientation and outer protection of a specific ODC wing are not published here. A coarse decorative weave is not a measured layup.

sources.title: Orbital Data Centers: Power Generation and Thermal Management as Architecture Drivers
sources.claim: The point design specifies silicon ROSA blankets and coated aluminum radiator face sheets. It names AZ-93 white paint as a coating example, and POCO foam or aluminum honeycomb as possible core fills.
sources.boundary: Aluminum face sheets are stated; paint product and core fill are examples, not a released bill of materials. A configured OSR surface is an explicit workbench adaptation. Cell maker, coverglass grade, alloys and detailed layups remain open.
sources.locator: Printed pages 8–9; Power Architecture and Thermal Architecture

sources.title: Space-Qualified Optical Solar Reflectors
sources.claim: The supplier specifies thin glass OSRs in CMX and CMO families, with distinct conductive and UV-reflective coating options and measured optical properties.
sources.boundary: CMX/CMO glass is not identified as fused silica by this data sheet. The workbench’s generic tiled glass-OSR depiction does not select this exact product, thickness, coating, tile pitch or qualification envelope.
sources.locator: One-page data sheet: Physical Properties and Typical Optical Solar Reflector Specifications

sources.title: Rocket Ranch — Some Like It Hot
sources.claim: NASA thermal researchers describe the established silver-and-quartz optical-solar-reflector approach.
sources.boundary: This is a generic material precedent. It does not turn every glass OSR into fused silica or identify the workbench’s selected product. The visible dielectric surface and reflective backing are distinct layers.

sources.title: AZ-93 White Thermal Control, Inorganic Paint / Coating
sources.claim: AZ-93 is a nonspecular white inorganic thermal-control coating with a silicate binder; the supplier publishes separate absorptance and emittance specifications.
sources.boundary: AZ-93 is a material-family benchmark. The active workbench paint selection and entered thermal properties are project assumptions unless an exact coating process and applicable life data are selected.

sources.title: AZ-93 Safety Data Sheet — CPS-C-001 Rev. F
sources.claim: The supplier identifies zinc oxide and potassium silicate among AZ-93 ingredients.
sources.boundary: The data sheet does not release formulation ratios. This establishes the coating family, not a reproducible paint recipe or a material selection for any ODC provider.

sources.title: Space Cells & Cell-Interconnect-Coverglass Assemblies
sources.claim: Spectrolab identifies its lattice-matched triple-junction family as GaInP/GaAs/Ge and offers assemblies including coverglass, bypass diodes and interconnects.
sources.boundary: A triple-junction texture represents the selected technology class. It does not establish a purchased cell, exact circuit pitch, flight efficiency or provider selection. Cell appearance is governed partly by coatings and coverglass.

sources.title: Space-Qualified Solar Cells
sources.claim: Sharp offers a silicon cell-interconnect-coverglass assembly alongside its multijunction products.
sources.boundary: This is a silicon-cell packaging precedent, not a claim that Sharp supplies a reference ODC. The supplier’s efficiency and life figures are not automatically adopted by the model.

sources.title: Inside a Solar Cell
sources.claim: ESA describes thin coverglass over space solar cells to reduce radiation damage, with the semiconductor and its interconnections beneath.
sources.boundary: Coverglass is an outer optical layer, not an opaque blue metal. Thickness, adhesive and radiation shielding require a cell-assembly selection; the article’s typical thickness is not a requirement for this design.

sources.title: Chemical Fabrication Used to Produce Thin-Film Materials for High Power-to-Weight-Ratio Space Photovoltaic Arrays
sources.claim: NASA discusses flexible polyimide substrates as a material class for lightweight space photovoltaic arrays.
sources.boundary: The cited research concerns thin-film arrays. It supports polyimide as a material precedent only; the workbench’s blanket backing, mesh reinforcement and roll-compatible construction remain allocations, not a reconstruction of ROSA or a supplier layup.

sources.title: Propellant Management Device Tanks
sources.claim: The manufacturer describes its PMD tank family as all-titanium for long-duration propellant compatibility.
sources.boundary: The MEL uses this family as a benchmark. Actual vessel selection, alloy, shell gauge, external finish and mounting design remain allocated. Bare titanium should not be rendered as gold foil unless a separate blanket is assigned.
sources.locator: Product-family description above PMD tank tables

sources.title: Pressurant Tanks
sources.claim: The supplier offers both monolithic titanium and composite-overwrapped pressure vessels for gases including helium.
sources.boundary: The family name alone cannot decide the installed bottle construction. Selecting either titanium or carbon overwrap is a project allocation until a matched vessel is identified.

sources.title: Juno Jupiter Orbit Insertion Press Kit — Electronics Vault
sources.claim: Juno uses a titanium electronics vault for its Jovian radiation environment.
sources.boundary: Titanium in the workbench is an explicitly inferred shielding material. Juno does not establish the LEO design’s thickness, dose attenuation, secondary-particle response or mass allocation.

sources.title: Deceptively Complex: Composite Overwrapped Pressure Vessels
sources.claim: NASA describes a pressure-retaining liner surrounded by a composite overwrap and discusses carbon-composite implementations.
sources.boundary: A wound-fiber depiction is appropriate only for an explicitly allocated COPV. It does not establish the liner material, fiber/resin system, winding schedule, pressure rating or life.

sources.title: 400 N Bipropellant Apogee Motors — S400-12 / S400-15
sources.claim: The supplier specifies a platinum-alloy chamber and throat for the S400 family, with film and radiative cooling.
sources.boundary: The table does not identify the entire expansion-bell alloy. A neutral metallic bell is a visual allocation with unresolved material, not evidence for niobium, carbon, steel or an all-platinum nozzle. The Aerozine study is not an S400 flight configuration.
sources.locator: Characteristics table: Chamber/Throat Material and Cooling Control

sources.title: PD-ED-1209 — Ammonia-Charged Aluminum Heat Pipes with Extruded Wicks
sources.claim: Goddard documents aluminum/ammonia heat-pipe practice and a metal/fluid compatibility table including aluminum and stainless steel with ammonia.
sources.boundary: This is a compatibility precedent, not qualification of the workbench pumped loop or heat-lift concept. Its near-room-temperature heat-pipe practice does not establish high-temperature refrigerant or seal suitability.

sources.title: 963-080-26 SpaceWire-Type Cable
sources.claim: This cable combines copper-alloy conductors, FEP insulation/jacket, aluminum-polyimide pair shielding and a silver-plated copper outer shield.
sources.boundary: Polyimide can be a buried shield layer; it is not necessarily the visible jacket. The workbench harness construction and exterior wrap are allocations, not a replica of this specific cable.

sources.title: Low-Profile Micro-D Connector Specifications
sources.claim: The supplier specifies copper-alloy contacts with gold over nickel, with different materials for the connector shell, insulator and mounting hardware.
sources.boundary: Gold is assigned only to small connector/contact details as a study finish. This does not select a flight connector or justify gold coloring for structural frames, pressure vessels or whole optical terminals.

sources.title: Beta Cloth
sources.claim: The supplier describes Beta cloth as PTFE-impregnated glass cloth used in spacecraft protection layers.
sources.boundary: A white woven protective cover is a material allocation, not evidence of a complete MMOD shield. Impact performance depends on the complete tested stack and its spacing.

sources.title: The Red Book — Revision E
sources.claim: The handbook distinguishes aluminized polymer films, glass-cloth covers and protective coatings, including separate exposed-metal and exposed-polymer optical behavior.
sources.boundary: Film orientation, substrate, thickness and added coatings matter. A blanket color or a texture cannot choose solar absorptance, thermal emittance, charging behavior or atomic-oxygen durability.
sources.locator: January 24, 2020 Revision E; Thermal Control Overview; MLI Blanket Materials

sources.title: Workmanship — Printed Circuit Board Product Assurance
sources.organization: NASA Office of Safety and Mission Assurance
sources.claim: NASA describes multiple PCB dielectric families and identifies glass-reinforced polyimide as a commonly used laminate for NASA applications.
sources.boundary: The COTS accelerator board laminate, copper stackup, solder mask and radiation capability are not established by this reference. Visible board details remain generic study representations.
sources.locator: PCB product assurance: laminate dielectric materials

sources.title: Fused-Silica Optical Windows and Broadband AR Coatings
sources.claim: The supplier describes fused-silica windows with wavelength-specific antireflection coatings for optical systems.
sources.boundary: This is a material/appearance precedent only. It does not identify the flight-terminal prescription, aperture window, spectral coating, glass grade or radiation performance. A subtle colored reflection is an illustrative coating response.

sources.title: Product Portfolio — S-Band TT&C Antenna
sources.claim: The S-band TT&C data sheet specifies a Vespel protective radome with SG121FD white paint on flight models.
sources.boundary: This is evidence for the cited benchmark antenna only. The workbench’s generic patch still has an unselected radome/paint system. Other Anywaves antenna products use different radome materials; a shared ivory texture does not identify polymer chemistry.
sources.locator: Printed page 7 / PDF page 7: Protective Radome row; compact variant on page 9 is separate
